Commentary.Commentary: We are back with action. The Lankan players are out in the middle. Shadman Islam and Anamul Haque to open for Bangladesh. Asitha Fernando to bowl first.
...THIRD INNINGS...

Earlier, Pathum Nissanka stole the show with his brilliant knock of 187 runs (his career-best Test score) and one, Sri Lanka needed from one of their top order. Dinesh Chandimal scored a fifty too while Angelo Mathews contributed as well but Bangladesh kept on chipping in with wickets while not much assist from the pitch. Now then, Bangladesh take a slender lead of 10 runs. Sri Lankan bowlers are well rested and will hope for a couple of wickets before the end of this session. Stay tuned.

Sri Lanka were in a top position when Milan Rathnayake and Kamindu Mendis were batting. It felt like the host will definitely take the lead but the pitch started to deteriorate a bit and Bangladesh made most of it with Hasan Mahmud and Nayeem Hasan sharing most of the wickets. Kamindu Mendis' wicket was the top story in this session as he was well set and closing on his century but Nayeem Hasan came up with a wonderful flighted delivery to get rid of him and eventually ending with a five-fer.

So, 980 runs scored in the two innings as we are halfway across Day 4 and we are yet to decide which team is on top. Bangladesh take a small margin lead of 10 runs with them. Bangladesh came into the second session with a lot of confidence as they took the last three wickets with just 15 runs on the board.

As we head into the second session, all eyes will be on whether this pair can continue their solid stand. Sri Lanka will look to build a lead from here, and if Kamindu gets to his hundred and Milan keeps supporting him well, they’ll be in a strong position. Bangladesh, on the flip side, will need a breakthrough early after lunch to wrest back control. The next hour or two could be crucial in shaping how this Test match moves forward. Join us at 7.10 am GMT for the next session!

Kamindu found a reliable partner in Milan Rathnayake, and the pair have added a valuable 79-run stand so far. Mendis is closing in on a well-deserved century, currently unbeaten on 83, while Milan is slowly but surely moving towards his second Test fifty. Their partnership has steadied the innings and helped Sri Lanka cut down the deficit without taking many risks. They've managed to keep Bangladesh’s bowlers at bay, setting the platform for a strong finish to the day.

Bangladesh had a strong start early in the day, removing two key batters, skipper Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis, within the first hour. It was a promising beginning, with Nayeem Hasan and Hasan Mahmud both picking up a wicket each and building good pressure. However, their momentum was halted by some calm and composed batting from Kamindu Mendis, who has looked in complete control and shown why he’s become such an important player for Sri Lanka in red-ball cricket in the last two years.

It was a balanced morning session with both sides having their moments. Sri Lanka managed to score 97 runs in 31 overs, while Bangladesh picked up two important wickets. The session could have tilted towards the visitors had they managed to dismiss Kamindu Mendis, who continues to stand firm at the crease. With Sri Lanka now trailing by just 30 runs, they’ll be feeling confident about taking the lead, but Bangladesh will know they missed a chance to apply more pressure, especially with the pitch looking easier to bat on as the day progresses.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Bangladesh have started well this first session with two big wickets of Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis, but Sri Lanka will be relying on their best batter of the last two years in this format, Kamindu Mendis, to bail them out from this position and get them past a lead on Day 4. The bowlers of Bangladesh are trying hard, and even though they have got two wickets early on but this pitch seems to be easing out now, and Sri Lanka can get benefitted from it if they bat sensibly from here. An interesting hour of play is ahead. Let's see how it goes. Also, Taijul Islam comes to attack for the first time today.

States that there are some footmarks of the bowlers, and it can get better for the batting.

With the weather holding up well on Day 3, fans will be hoping for another uninterrupted day of cricket. The fourth day could well define the trajectory of this Test - will Sri Lanka take control, or can Bangladesh bounce back with the ball? All the answers lie ahead, so don’t go anywhere. Stay tuned.

Bangladesh, meanwhile, have the second new ball just a few overs old, and they’ll be hoping the morning conditions offer them some help off the surface. But they’ll need to tighten their lines and apply consistent pressure if they’re to make inroads into the Sri Lankan middle and lower order. The match is delicately poised, but at this stage, Sri Lanka appear to have a slight edge. A strong session with the bat could see them turn that into a commanding position.

Pathum Nissanka grabbed the headlines on Day 3 as he scored his career-best Test score and was the centre of the action as Sri Lanka started their journey to notch up a big second innings score. The likes of Dinesh Chandimal and Angelo Mathews played their part, but Nissanka showed how good a pitch this is to play on and batted almost the entire of Day 3 before getting out in the final hour of the day. Also, we’re set for an early start today, 15 minutes ahead, to make up for time lost earlier in the match.

Hello and welcome, everyone, for the action of Day 4 between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh from Galle. The tempo at which Sri Lanka played on moving Day 3 just shows they want a result out of this rather than settling for a draw. The hosts scored 368 compared to Bangladesh’s 495 and trail by just 127 runs. If they show a similar kind of approach, they’ll be close to taking the lead but have to rely on Kamindu Mendis and skipper Dhananjaya de Silva to score the bulk of the runs.

Bangladesh had a tiring day in the field with the pitch supporting the batters mostly. The spinners tried to bowl in the rough to extract some spin but with the Lankans' heavily dominated right-handed middle order, it was of no use. Bangladesh though got the big wicket of Pathum Nissanka soon after taking the second new ball. It's just around 7 overs old, so Bangladesh will hope to try and dominate the first hour of Day 4 with it. Day 4 could give us the most important moments of the game and surely you wouldn't want to miss it. Join us at 4.15 am GMT for the action of Day 4 and earlier for the build up. Earlier in the day, Sri Lanka needed just one wicket to close out Bangladesh's innings and they did the job very quickly. In reply, Sri Lanka added 100 runs in the first session while losing Lahiru Udara in the process. The second session was thoroughly dominated by Sri Lanka as they added another 133 runs to the total, thanks to some clean hitting from Pathum Nissanka, who was well supported by Dinesh Chandimal and Sri Lanka's stalwart Angelo Mathews. Angelo Mathews, who is playing his farewell Test, was greeted with a guard of honour from the Bangladesh players however, the all-rounder couldn't convert his good start into a big score.

Sri Lanka end Day 3 on a high as, session by session, they increased their run rate but Bangladesh will be slightly relieved after taking the big wicket of Pathum Nissanka in the final hour of the day. Pathum Nissanka was the highlight of the day for his wonderful knock of 187, which have helped Sri Lanka cut the deficit more than half and only trail by 127 runs as we move to Day 4.
